class.name: NNSTNodes
class.brief_description: A state management structure that is a hybrid of a behaviour tree and a hierarchical state machine.
class.description: A StateTree is a state management structure that is a hybrid of a behaviour tree and a hierarchical state machine. The State Tree consists of five concrete node types ([NNSTRoot], [NNSTNode], [NNSTParallel], [NNSTTransition], and [NNSTHistory]) together with [NNSTGuard] resources ([NNSTExpressionGuard], [NNSTStateIsActiveGuard], [NNSTAllOfGuard], [NNSTAnyOfGuard], and [NNSTNotGuard]) for gating transitions. State Tree nodes are utility-enabled, which means that if desired, child state selection can be done by using [NNConsideration] nodes. Alternatively, an [method NNSTTickedNodes.on_enter_condition] method can be defined on state nodes to define the selection logic. When the tree is ticked for the first time, a set of active states is selected by evaluating the child nodes of the root node, and the childs of the child nodes, until a leaf node is found that can be activated (i.e. its [method NNSTTickedNodes.on_enter_condition] method returns [code]true[/code] or utility-based evaluation selects it as the highest-scoring node). All the State Tree nodes from the root node all the way down to the found leaf node are then considered as "active". On subsequent calls to the root node [method NNSTRoot.tick] method, all the active nodes are ticked in top-to-down order from the root to the leaf node. This allows you to create a hierarchy of states with shared logic on the top-level nodes and more specific logic on the leaf nodes. You can select the child node evaluation method for each branch node by setting the [member NNSTBranchNodes.child_state_selection_rule] property. User-defined methods [code]on_enter_condition() -> bool[/code], [code]on_enter_state()[/code], [code]on_exit_state()[/code] and [code]on_tick(delta)[/code] can be defined to create your custom state activation and handling logic. State data lives in the [NNBlackboard] of the nearest root of any Noodle Nodes system and is reached with the [method NoodleNodes.get_blackboard], [method NoodleNodes.set_blackboard], [method NoodleNodes.has_blackboard], [method NoodleNodes.erase_blackboard], [method NoodleNodes.get_blackboard_resource] and [method NoodleNodes.get_actor] helpers. Alternatively, you can also use the signals [signal NNSTTickedNodes.state_check_enter_condition], [signal NNSTTickedNodes.state_entered], [signal NNSTTickedNodes.state_exited] and [signal NNSTTickedNodes.state_ticked]. States are changed by calling [method NNSTTickedNodes.transition_to] with a [NodePath] relative to the calling node, or through [NNSTTransition] nodes (via [method NNSTBranchNodes.send_event], [method NNSTTransition.take], or automatic triggers). The target path may point to any [NNSTNode] or [NNSTParallel] state in the State Tree (other than the calling state itself, its descendants, a state across an [NNSTParallel] common ancestor, or an exiting lineage), or to an [NNSTHistory] node to restore a compound state's remembered or default state. When the target state is entered, its child states are evaluated down the tree (or restored from history). If the transition cannot be applied, [method NNSTTickedNodes.transition_to] returns [code]false[/code] and the State Tree remains in its existing state. [b]Note:[/b] When a scene with a State Tree is first run, during the first call to the tick() method the State Tree will automatically transition to the root node to find the initial set of active states. When the state changes, the [code]on_exit_state()[/code] method is called for existing state nodes that are not included in the new state set. Similarly, for new state nodes that were not included in the existing state set, the [code]on_enter_state()[/code] method is called. During a tick, the [code]on_tick()[/code] method is called for all the active states. You construct a State Tree by first adding an [NNSTRoot] node to your scene. Under the root node you add concrete state nodes ([NNSTNode] and [NNSTParallel]) and nest further states as needed, along with [NNSTTransition] children for transitions and [NNSTHistory] children on compound [NNSTNode] states for history.
